paragraphs.title: David’s Victories over the Philistines, Moab, and Aram

easy.explanation: The first verse says that David smote and subdued the Philistines.
easy.q: Whom did David subdue at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: David took Metheg-ammah out of the hand of the Philistines.
easy.q: What did David take from the Philistines?

easy.explanation: The Syrians of Damascus came to succour Hadadezer king of Zobah.

answers: The Moabites became David’s servants and brought gifts
Moab became an equal ally of David
medium.explanation: The Moabites became David’s servants and brought gifts.
medium.q: What was the result of David’s battle against Moab?

answers: Military outposts or governing posts established in a land
medium.explanation: David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus, meaning that he established positions of control there.
medium.q: What does the word “garrisons” mean in this passage?

answers: David defeated it and put garrisons there
Toi king of Hamath gave it to David
The Philistines asked it to surrender
medium.explanation: David slew the Syrians and then put garrisons in Syria of Damascus.
medium.q: What caused Syria of Damascus to become subject to David?

answers: He disabled most of Hadadezer’s chariot force
He gave the chariots to Syria of Damascus
challenge.explanation: David houghed the chariot horses but reserved enough horses for one hundred chariots.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that David reserved one hundred chariots after houg​​hing the chariot horses?

answers: Military victories, establishment of garrisons, and receipt of gifts
Receipt of gifts, retreat, and establishment of garrisons
Establishment of garrisons, defeat, and independence
challenge.explanation: The passage presents victories first, garrisons next, and submission with gifts afterward.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the spread of David’s rule in this passage?

answers: The LORD preserved David wherever he went
The LORD told David to stop fighting
The LORD gave Jerusalem to Aram
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went.
challenge.q: What does the passage say about the Lord’s role in David’s victories?

easy.explanation: David took the shields of gold that were on Hadadezer’s servants.
easy.q: What did David take from the servants of Hadadezer?

easy.explanation: David brought the golden shields to Jerusalem.
easy.q: Where did David bring the golden shields?

easy.explanation: Toi sent Joram his son unto king David.

answers: To salute him and bless him
medium.explanation: Joram was sent to salute David and bless him because David had fought against Hadadezer.
medium.q: Why did Toi send Joram to David?

medium.explanation: Joram brought vessels of silver, gold, and brass.

answers: He dedicated them unto the LORD
He divided them among the Syrians
He used them to build a new army
medium.explanation: David dedicated these materials unto the LORD.
medium.q: What did David do with the silver, gold, and brass he received or took?

answers: He set them apart for sacred use unto the LORD
He hid them from the people
He returned them all to his enemies
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes that David dedicated the silver, gold, and other spoils unto the LORD.
challenge.q: What does David’s act of dedication reveal about his attitude toward the spoils of war?

answers: The victory caused Toi to send his son to bless David
The visit caused David to fight Hadadezer
The victory caused Joram to appoint David as a priest
challenge.explanation: Toi heard that David had smitten Hadadezer and therefore sent Joram to him.
challenge.q: What was the connection between David’s victory over Hadadezer and Joram’s visit?

answers: The passage mentions golden shields, vessels, and spoil from several nations
Only gifts from Toi are mentioned
challenge.explanation: The passage lists shields, vessels, and spoil from Syria, Moab, Ammon, the Philistines, Amalek, and Hadadezer.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the dedicated treasures came from different sources?

easy.explanation: The passage says that David smote the Syrians in the Valley of Salt.
easy.q: Whom did David smite in the Valley of Salt?

easy.explanation: David put garrisons throughout all Edom.
All they of Edom became David’s servants.
easy.q: What was the result of David’s rule over Edom?

answers: The victory caused David to get a name
The victory caused David to lose his name
The victory caused Edom to get a name
medium.explanation: David got him a name when he returned from smiting the Syrians in the Valley of Salt.
medium.q: What was the connection between the victory in the Valley of Salt and David’s name?

answers: Edom was subject to David’s rule
medium.explanation: The phrase describes Edom’s subjection to David after he put garrisons there.
medium.q: What does “David’s servants” mean in this context?

answers: He went to rule in Hamath
medium.explanation: After the victory, David put garrisons throughout all Edom.
medium.q: What did David do after his victory over the Syrians?

answers: Establishing garrisons and making Edom subject to him
Making an equal treaty and placing no officials there
challenge.explanation: The passage links the establishment of garrisons with Edom becoming David’s servants.
challenge.q: Which combination describes David’s method of ruling Edom?

answers: His successes were also attributed to the LORD’s help
The garrisons acted without connection to David
challenge.explanation: The verse ends by saying that the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went.
challenge.q: What does the repeated statement about the LORD preserving David emphasize?

answers: Victory over Syria, David’s fame, and garrisons in Edom
Garrisons in Edom, defeat by Syria, and David’s fame
David’s fame, Israel’s surrender, and war in Edom
challenge.explanation: The passage presents the victory first, David’s name next, and the garrisons in Edom afterward.
challenge.q: Which sequence is correct according to the passage?

paragraphs.title: David’s Kingship and Administration of Justice

easy.explanation: The verse says that David reigned over all Israel.

answers: He took spoil from them only
He appointed them to the army
easy.explanation: David executed judgment and justice unto all his people.
easy.q: What did David do for the people?

answers: The kings of other nations only
easy.explanation: The verse specifically says, “unto all his people.”
easy.q: To whom did David execute judgment and justice?

answers: His rule included fairness and righteous judgment
He gave up governing the people
medium.explanation: The verse describes David as a king who executed judgment and justice.
medium.q: What does the phrase “judgment and justice” reveal about David’s leadership?

answers: Justice was presented as part of his reign
Justice occurred only before he became king
Justice was administered by enemy kings
medium.explanation: The same verse says that David reigned over Israel and executed judgment and justice.
medium.q: What was the relationship between David’s reign and his administration of justice?

answers: His rule is described as extending over the whole nation
His rule was limited to one city
His rule was limited to the priests
medium.explanation: The word “all” indicates the full extent of David’s rule over Israel.
medium.q: What can be understood from the word “all” in “all Israel”?

answers: “Reigned over all Israel” and “executed judgment and justice”
challenge.explanation: The verse joins the extent of David’s kingship with the manner in which he governed.
challenge.q: Which phrase presents both royal authority and moral responsibility?

answers: His administration was not limited to one particular group
He cared only for his army
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that David acted for all his people.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that judgment and justice were given to all the people?

answers: David was king over all Israel and a ruler who executed judgment and justice
David was an army captain under another king
David was a messenger who brought gifts to Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: This is the direct meaning of II Samuel 8:15.
challenge.q: Which statement most accurately summarizes the verse?

easy.explanation: Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the host.
Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was the recorder.
The passage says, “Seraiah was the scribe.”

answers: Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar
medium.explanation: Zadok and Ahimelech are named together as the priests.
Benaiah was over both the Cherethites and the Pelethites.
medium.q: What was Benaiah the son of Jehoiada over?

medium.explanation: The passage ends by saying that David’s sons were chief rulers.
medium.q: What is said about David’s sons?

answers: Military command, administration, priesthood, writing, and special forces
challenge.explanation: The list includes commanders, a recorder, priests, a scribe, and leaders of the Cherethites and Pelethites.
challenge.q: Which areas of government are represented in the list of officials?

challenge.explanation: The passage identifies Jehoshaphat as recorder and Seraiah as scribe.
challenge.q: Which pair matches the correct people and offices?

answers: David had an organized government with distinct offices
All the officials performed the same task
challenge.explanation: The verses identify separate military, administrative, priestly, and scribal roles.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the detailed list of officials?
